questions: Must the plant also meet all demand during an unplanned winter doublet outage? The cheapest tested design meets demand with planned, staggered shutdowns but fails that winter-outage test. (If you do not know: Use planned, staggered shutdowns; explicitly report the limitation for unplanned winter outages..)
final_reply:
The cheapest tested design is €38.39/MWh of delivered heating and cooling, costing €5.198 million/year. [R0353]

It uses two 3,175 m doublets, CHP burning the co-produced gas, a screw chiller with dry cooler, and a 0.2 MW ORC power unit. Heating and cooling return temperatures are 45°C and 30°C. Capital cost is €41.70 million. [R0353]

It meets all demand and hard rules with planned, staggered shutdowns, and GEMINI Solver agrees at both demand peaks. [R0353] It has no backup boiler and fails the unplanned winter-outage test. [R0426]

Screening covered doublet counts, depths, heating and coolin
